meiotic CO/NCO designation is regulated by crossover interference and that this occurs prior to the formation of stable recombination intermediates and synapsis.

(1) CO/NCO designation is an early meiotic event that occurs well before stable strand exchange; (2) CO/NCO designations are regulated to ensure that the number of COs is limited and that they are distributed evenly along chromosomes; and (3) CO/NCO and synapsis occur in a sequential manner, with synapsis occurring after CO/NCO design.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the early stages of meiosis in yeast and plants.
the molecular mechanism of early meiotic CO interference in budding yeast and its relationship with synapsis.
the early stages of meiotic recombination and the role of synapsis in the process.

the CO/NCO decision occurs prior to synapsis, but after the initial steps of stable strand exchange.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
COs are designated prior to synapsis and that synapsis is required for CO interference.
CO interference is established before synapsis and is independent of synapsis.
CO/NCO designation is an early meiotic decision that occurs prior to synapsis and that CO/NCO distribution is regulated before stable strand exchange.
The main takeaway from our work is that
meiotic crossover interference occurs prior to synapsis.
meiotic recombination is regulated at multiple stages, and these regulations are independent of one another.
